title: Projection coherence and domains at finite and tower coefficients
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be smooth separated morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and put $h=gf$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Use either a finite commutative ring $B=A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, with the ordinary constant-$A$ pro-etale derived categories and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [det-sp-finite-general-ring], or $B=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_{n\ge1}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, in the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. In the latter case $\mathcal C_T(B)$ is the full subcategory with cohomology and Tor intervals uniform in $n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]; input towers need not be normalized. All tensors are ordinary derived tensors over $B$, with derived pullback, shifts and twists [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For $u=f,g,h$ use $F_u=Ru_{!,B}\dashv G_u=u_B^!$, its counit $\varepsilon_u$, and $\omega_u=G_uB_{\mathrm{target}(u)}$ [def-pur-co-smoothness, det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gluing, det-sp-tower-gamma]. Let $\alpha:F_gF_f\simeq F_h$ and $c:G_h\simeq G_fG_g$ be the counit-preserving comparisons [det-sp-composition-comparisons].

The schemes are Noetherian and the maps $f,g,h$ admit compactifications. The composite has relative dimension $d+e$. For every $K\in\mathcal C_Z(B)$ the objects $\omega_g$, $G_gK$ and $W=f^*\omega_g\otimes\omega_f$ lie in the corresponding constructible finite-Tor categories. Each $\omega_u$ is isomorphic to $B(d_u)[2d_u]$; tensoring with its unshifted Tate line preserves any Tor interval $[a,b]$, and the shift changes it to $[a-2d_u,b-2d_u]$, uniformly for towers.

Write $P_{u,M,L}:F_uM\otimes L\to F_u(M\otimes u^*L)$ for the canonical compactification projection, obtained from open extension and the proper counit projection. On the displayed constructible finite-Tor inputs these maps are invertible, natural, unital, and satisfy
$$P_{h,M,L}(\alpha_M\otimes1)=\alpha_{M\otimes f^*g^*L}\,F_g(P_{f,M,g^*L})P_{g,F_fM,L},$$
$$P_{u,M,L\otimes L'}=P_{u,M\otimes u^*L,L'}(P_{u,M,L}\otimes1),$$
with the canonical pullback and tensor associators. Both equalities hold in the coefficient derived categories themselves, before tower evaluation. At finite $A$, they use the pro-etale maps transported from the ordinary etale compactification maps; the site comparison preserves this same $\alpha$ and the counits. At towers they use the simultaneous section-model maps with their actual quotient transitions. Under $(\varpi_E^{en})=(\ell^n)$, where $e$ is the ramification index, restriction of the uniformizer-indexed models to indices $en$ identifies their projection and composition maps with these $\ell$-indexed maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$; a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus $X,Y,Z$ are Noetherian. The setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] applies verbatim and supplies compactifications, with separated finite-type middle schemes, of every map used here. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2), $h$ is smooth of dimension $d+e$, including on empty schemes. Fix these compactifications and the comparisons of [det-sp-composition-comparisons]. Their normalization is precisely the proper/open compositor and its adjunction comparison, with composite counit $\varepsilon_gF_g(\varepsilon_fG_g)$; it is not an independently chosen isomorphism. Lean geometry is proved directly: isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType gives the three Noetherian instances; the published compactifiability theorem [def-asd-compactifiable] gives the three compactifications; Mathlib's smoothOfRelativeDimension_comp supplies dimension d+e. No chosen comparison is needed for this geometric conjunction.

For finite $A$, [det-sp-finite-general-ring](1),(3), applied to $f,g,h$, identifies $\omega_u$ with $A(d_u)[2d_u]$ and $G_gK$ with $g^*K(e)[2e]$. The Tate lines of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] are locally free of rank one; their pro-etale realizations remain locally free. The finite pullback assertion of [lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains] gives constructibility and boundedness of $f^*\omega_g$. Locally tensoring with a Tate line is tensoring with $A$, hence is exact and preserves the Tor interval of every tensor test. Applying the inverse line proves preservation in both directions. Since $H^i(C[s])=H^{i+s}(C)$, a shift by $2d_u$ subtracts $2d_u$ from both endpoints. Thus $W=f^*\omega_g\otimes\omega_f$ is a shifted tensor product of two locally free rank-one constructible sheaves, hence is constructible finite-Tor. This also verifies the domain for $G_gK$; no DVR presentation of $A$ is used. The restricted adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] also ensures that every finite compact-support image, in particular $F_fM$ in the composite formula, is ctf. Lean finite_domains uses the proved private ordinary-origin, comparison, and smooth-exceptional preservation helpers in [lem-pur-finite-smooth-level-of-orientation]. The ordinary coefficient unit is transported through smoothPurityUnitIso and the exact comparison. Applying smooth-exceptional preservation for g gives omega_g and G_g K. The proved smooth tensor-domain helper of [lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains], applied to f with input omega_g, gives W. This needs no new orientation calculation. The orientation/Tor-interval clause itself retains the preceding plan and remains unproved in this delivery.

For towers, use [det-sp-tower-gamma](1),(2) for the actual orientation isomorphisms and $G_gK\simeq g^*K(e)[2e]$. The tower clause of [lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains] preserves the common cohomological and Tor intervals under pullback, without normalization. The line calculation in Step 2 applies at every $n$ with the same interval endpoints and the same shift. Consequently $\omega_g$, $G_gK$ and $W$ have common cohomological and Tor bounds and constructible levels. For example $\omega_u$ has Tor interval $[-2d_u,-2d_u]$ and $W$ has $[-2(d+e),-2(d+e)]$. These are statements about intervals containing the support; no nonzero cohomology is asserted for an empty scheme or zero object. The uniform tower category is exactly the full subcategory specified in [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. The tower functors in [det-sp-composition-comparisons](3) are defined on these uniform ctf subcategories, so the intermediate compact-support inputs in the composite identity also stay in that domain. Lean tower_domains needs only the full-subcategory membership of the outputs of the supplied right adjoints: transport their property fields through the unit of the fixed realization equivalence. Pullback membership follows from the proved tower_pullback_mem helper in [lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains]. Apply [lem-sp-uniform-tower-tensor-closure] to the pulled-back omega_g and omega_f, then transport the tensor through the realization counit. This proves all three domain assertions without normalization or smooth orientation. The explicit orientation and interval clause retains the preceding plan and remains unproved.

In the finite case [lem-sp-finite-ring-compact-support-projection] constructs $P$ as the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor map, and proves its invertibility and naturality on bounded constructible inputs. To compare with etale maps, choose bounded constructible etale origins by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-finite-ring-site-tensor-transpose] identifies the actual projection arrows through the compact-support comparison, and clause (1) identifies the counits. The composition equation of [lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence] identifies that comparison with the very same proper/open $\alpha$ fixed in Step 1. Thus this transport changes neither the projection nor the compositor. Substituting these comparisons into [lem-amb-compactification-projection-composition] gives the first displayed identity, with exactly $\alpha_{M\otimes f^*g^*L}$ on the right. The latter lemma holds for arbitrary finite $A$ and arbitrary unbounded etale inputs, so all our witnesses satisfy its hypotheses.

For tower inputs use [lem-sp-strict-compactification-comparison-realization]: $P^c=G_p(\gamma)\pi_p$ is an actual transformation on ordinary unbounded varying-coefficient towers; $\pi_p$ is the counit transpose and $\gamma$ has the open-unit normalization. This is the same word as the finite $P$, with the actual quotient transitions. On the stated uniform ctf inputs it is invertible by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a). Indeed the towers are bounded below; every finite ring $A_n$ is Noetherian, and [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies bounded constructible finite-Tor etale origins for their levels on our qcqs Noetherian schemes. No compatible choice of these origins is required by (2a). The arbitrary-strict-system clause of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] now gives the first displayed equality directly in the system derived category. Its proper/open maps are the same simultaneous maps: [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting] specifies them as the clopen-projector mates, with their horizontal and vertical pastings before evaluation. The system category here is literally the semilinear category of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; no normalized-system restriction is made in the cited composition clause. Its compositor is the geometric one of Step 1, not a lift chosen from its evaluations.

Here is the tensor-variable identity in either coefficient case. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition] on the ordinary ringed site, or on its ringed sequence site, whose module category is [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. It gives the tensor-associativity equation for $\pi_p$. For the open factor, [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] makes $j^*\gamma$ the identity and makes $j_!$ fully faithful. Both iterated open tensor maps are therefore the same: apply $j^*$ and the canonical associators to obtain the identity on $M\otimes j^*N\otimes j^*N'$. Their sources are in the image of $j_!$ via $\gamma$, so full faithfulness applies. Write $P_{M,L}=Rp_*(\gamma_{M,p^*L})\pi_{p,j_!M,L}$. In the product $P_{M\otimes j^*p^*L,L'}(P_{M,L}\otimes1)$, naturality of $\pi_p$ at $\gamma_{M,p^*L}$ moves this open map inside $Rp_*$. The proper tensor-associativity equation combines the two $\pi_p$ factors, and the just-proved open equation combines the two $\gamma$ factors. The result is $Rp_*(\gamma_{M,p^*(L\otimes L')})\pi_{p,j_!M,L\otimes L'}=P_{M,L\otimes L'}$. Pullback tensor comparisons and associators are the canonical monoidal ones of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. This proves the second displayed identity on actual system maps, rather than testing equality after evaluation.

source.place: (2), associativity of tensor products and open/proper factors

proof.text: Naturality of $P$ follows from naturality of its two factors. For its coefficient-unit constraint, the transpose of $\pi_{p,E,1}$, after the canonical pullback/unit identifications of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], is $\varepsilon_{p,E}$. The adjunct of $1_{Rp_*E}$ is the same counit, so injectivity of adjunction transposition gives $\pi_{p,E,1}=1$. The open-unit normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] likewise gives $\gamma_{M,1}=1$ after unit identifications. Hence $P_{u,M,1}=1$. This proves the asserted unitality in the finite and sequence sites alike.

It remains to check the arithmetic index convention on these maps. Write the ramification index as $r$ here, to distinguish it from the relative dimension of $g$. Let $U$ retain indices $rn$ of the $\varpi_E$-system. By [lem-sp-arithmetic-system-right-adjoint], $U$ has the exact floor-extension right adjoint $J$ with $UJ=1$. Restriction is exact and computes its own derived functor; [lem-pur-system-derived-subsequence] identifies its cochain localization and selected evaluations. It is monoidal before derivation, since tensor and its relations are componentwise. It also preserves K-flat complexes: for an acyclic selected-system complex $C$, $JC$ is acyclic, and $U(P\otimes JC)=UP\otimes C$; thus the right side is acyclic when $P$ is K-flat. Consequently the derived tensor/pullback comparisons restrict with their actual associators. Here $U$ is also ringed direct image for the index-selection morphism of sequence topoi (its underlying left adjoint is ceiling-index extension). The two composites with a geometric direct image are identical already on sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to these two factorizations to obtain $U Rp_*\simeq Rp_* U$. Open extension and geometric inverse image commute termwise with $U$. The adjunction-compatibility and monoidal-composition clauses of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] identify these as counit-preserving comparisons, so they carry the defining word $Rp_*(\gamma)\pi_p$ and the proper/open compositor to the corresponding restricted words. Thus they identify projection and composition as actual derived transformations.

source.place: (2), uniformizer-indexed simultaneous models and arithmetic restriction

proof.text: Finally $\ell=u\varpi_E^r$ implies equality of ideals $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{rn})$. The identity on $\mathcal O_E$ therefore identifies their quotient rings and every quotient transition; explicitly both reductions send the class of $x$ to the class of $x$. This is the commuting quotient diagram of [lem-sp-cofinal-coefficient-projection-cocone], with $q_{n,rn}$ an isomorphism. Applying this ring-system identification to Step 8 gives precisely the $\ell$-indexed simultaneous models of [lem-sp-strict-compactification-comparison-realization]. The projection and composition words are unchanged. All tower equalities above were proved in their derived categories; joint evaluation conservativity was used only for invertibility where the cited projection theorem uses it, never for equality of maps.

source.place: (2), equality of the ramified quotient models

proof.text: Compactification choices. Steps 4 and 5 form $P_h$ and the compositor with the composite compactification of $h$, whereas Step 1 fixed $c_h$; the two are compared through a common refinement [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered], and the $\alpha$ of [det-sp-composition-comparisons] includes exactly these refinement comparisons. At finite $A$, [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] states the first displayed identity for the compactification-independent etale functors and their tower-normalized compositor, including compatibility with the refinement comparisons; the refinement equation of [lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence] and the transport of Step 4 carry it to the pro-etale maps, tensor symmetry ordering the factors. For towers, [lem-sf-refinement-projection-counit] gives $C_u(K\otimes P_hL)\,\mathrm{PF}^{c_2}_{K,L}=\mathrm{PF}^{c_1}_{K,L}(C_uK\otimes1)$ for every refinement $u$, in the system category before evaluation. On our bounded-below inputs $C_u$ is invertible: its evaluations are the finite refinement isomorphisms [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence] and evaluation is conservative [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](3). Conjugating the identity of Step 5 by these $C_u$ gives it for $c_h$; Steps 8 and 9 carry the refinement maps to the $\ell$-indexed models with the other proper/open words. Steps 6 and 7 hold for each compactification separately.
